dedupe_keys.name: lazio italy discrete event simulation of ambulance home bases for the ares 118 regional emergency medical service

description: This case study builds a discrete event simulation of a regional ambulance emergency system and applies it to a territory served by ARES 118, the regional emergency medical services authority of Lazio, Italy. The authors, from Italian universities, published it as a 41-page preprint. The model reproduces the stochastic workflow of calls, dispatch, travel to the scene, on-scene care, transport to an emergency department and return, and integrates data collected from several sources. The area studied contains a medium-size city and sparsely populated surroundings. The preprint is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the exact territory, data periods and parameters are only as described in the preprint, it has not been peer reviewed, and the model code is not reported as public. The authors report that the model reproduces the operation of the ambulance system very accurately and use scenario analyses of ambulance home base deployment to show how managers can improve the effectiveness and speed of the regional system. Simulation uses: a worked example of discrete event simulation for emergency response capacity planning and base location optimisation, reusable for disruption scenarios. Related records: the NHS ambulance DES (model-ambulance-des-nhsx) and the Iceland helicopter base study (case_study-iceland-helicopter-ambulance-base-location) take comparable approaches.
